name: Firecrawl
tagline: Web data API that turns websites into clean, LLM-ready markdown, JSON, and search results.
description: Firecrawl is a web crawling, scraping, and search API built for AI applications. It converts URLs to clean markdown, HTML, screenshots, or structured JSON via a single API call, handling JavaScript rendering and proxies automatically. The project is open source with a large community, and the hosted version adds an interact mode for operating pages and an MCP server for agent integrations.
pricing_details: Free tier includes 1,000 pages/month. Paid plans: Hobby $16/mo (5,000 pages), Standard $83/mo (100,000 pages), Growth $333/mo (500,000 pages), Scale $599/mo (1M credits), Enterprise custom; prices are annual-billing equivalents.
use_cases: Feeding web pages into RAG pipelines as clean markdown
Powering deep-research agents with search and scrape
Crawling entire sites for structured data extraction
Lead enrichment and competitive intelligence
Giving coding agents web access via MCP
pros: Open source core with very large community adoption
Clean markdown output reduces token usage for LLMs
Handles JS-heavy pages without configuration
Official MCP server and multi-language SDKs
cons: Credit system makes costs hard to predict at scale
No pay-per-use option; credits mostly do not roll over
Advanced features consume extra credits per call
who_its_for: AI engineers building agents and RAG pipelines
Developers needing web data without maintaining scrapers
Data teams doing large-scale extraction
Startups shipping AI features on live web data
key_features: Scrape, crawl, map, search, and interact endpoints
LLM-ready markdown and structured JSON output
Automatic JavaScript rendering and smart wait
Official MCP server and CLI for agent setup
SDKs for Python, Node, Go, Rust, Java, and Elixir
Open-source core with hosted enterprise options

name: Context.dev
tagline: Web scraping and brand data API for AI agents, turning any URL into markdown or structured data.
description: Context.dev is a developer API that scrapes URLs, crawls sites, and extracts structured data such as markdown, HTML, sitemaps, screenshots, and brand assets (logos, colors, fonts). It targets AI products and agents, offering self-serve API keys, SDKs, and quick integration. Customers include Mintlify, daily.dev, and DocsBot, mainly for onboarding enrichment and agent features.
pricing_details: Free plan with 500 API credits and no credit card required. Paid plans listed on the pricing page: Developer $25/mo, Pro $149/mo, Scale $499/mo, with a custom Enterprise tier for teams needing more than 2M credits per month.
use_cases: Enriching SaaS onboarding with brand data from a URL
Giving AI agents the ability to read web pages
Crawling sites for markdown content at scale
Extracting logos, colors, and company info automatically
Powering enrichment and automation features in AI products
pros: Self-serve signup with immediate API key
Combines scraping and brand intelligence under one key
No credit card needed to test the API
Thorough documentation with 10-minute integration reported by users
cons: Smaller credit allotments than some scraping competitors
Brand data focus may be unnecessary for pure scraping needs
Relatively young product with a smaller track record
who_its_for: SaaS founders adding URL-based onboarding enrichment
AI product teams building agents that read the web
Developers wanting a single API for scrape plus brand data
Startups replacing in-house scraping infrastructure
key_features: URL-to-markdown scraping and full-site crawling
Brand data API: logos, colors, fonts, company info
Structured extraction with AI
Self-serve API keys and developer SDKs
Screenshots, sitemaps, and HTML output
Usage-based credit system across all endpoints

name: Zernio
tagline: One API to publish, message, advertise, and analyze across 15 social and messaging platforms.
description: Zernio is a unified social media and messaging API for developers and AI agents. It covers publishing, scheduling, analytics, DMs, comments, and ad boosting across 15 channels including Instagram, TikTok, X, LinkedIn, YouTube, WhatsApp, and Bluesky, using official platform APIs. It also provides WhatsApp business numbers with KYC handled, and ships an MCP server so agents can post and manage accounts in natural language.
pricing_details: Usage-based per connected account: first 2 accounts free (no card), then $6/account/mo for accounts 3-10, $3/account/mo for 11-100, and $1/account/mo for 101+. X/Twitter API calls, phone numbers, calls, and SMS are billed separately at pass-through rates.
use_cases: Adding social publishing to a SaaS product without building 15 integrations
Letting AI agents post and reply to DMs via MCP
Scheduling content across all major platforms from one call
Running unified analytics for many client accounts
Provisioning WhatsApp business numbers programmatically
pros: Single OAuth flow and API across 15 channels
Uses only official platform APIs, avoiding account bans
Transparent graduated per-account pricing with a real free tier
MCP server with 280+ tools for agent workflows
cons: Developer-oriented; requires API skills or no-code connectors
X/Twitter usage costs extra at pass-through rates
Per-account billing can add up for agencies with many clients
who_its_for: Developers building social features into products
Agencies managing many client social accounts
Teams adding WhatsApp messaging without regulatory paperwork
Builders wiring AI agents to social channels
key_features: Unified posting, scheduling, and analytics across 15 platforms
Single OAuth connection flow, no per-platform dev apps
Unified inbox for DMs, comments, and reviews
Ad boosting across multiple ad networks
WhatsApp number provisioning with KYC handled
MCP server for natural-language agent control

name: Peec AI
tagline: AI search analytics tracking how brands appear in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and other AI answers.
description: Peec AI is a Berlin-based platform that measures brand visibility, position, and sentiment in AI-generated search answers across models like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews. Marketing teams track prompts, citations, and competitors with daily refresh, and export reporting via Looker Studio or API. It is used by over a thousand brands and agencies and has raised about $29M in venture funding.
pricing_details: Brand plans: Starter $95/mo (50 prompts, 1 project), Pro $245/mo (150 prompts, 2 projects), Advanced $495/mo (350 prompts, 5 projects), Enterprise custom; agency plans from $245/mo. Annual billing saves about 15%, and a 7-day free trial is offered.
use_cases: Monitoring brand mentions in AI search answers
Tracking prompt-level visibility versus competitors
Measuring sentiment and position in LLM responses
Reporting AI visibility to clients via Looker Studio
Informing GEO (generative engine optimization) strategy
pros: Purpose-built for AI search visibility rather than retrofitted SEO metrics
Unlimited users on every plan
Daily tracking cadence on all self-serve tiers
Strong multi-country and multilingual coverage
cons: Only 3 AI models included per plan; extra models cost more
Monitoring-focused, with limited built-in optimization guidance
Higher entry price than some newer competitors
who_its_for: Marketing and SEO teams at mid-size to enterprise brands
Agencies reporting AI visibility to multiple clients
Growth teams building a GEO practice
Global brands needing multi-market tracking
key_features: Prompt tracking across major AI search models
Visibility, position, and sentiment metrics
Competitor share-of-voice comparisons
Daily data refresh on all plans
Looker Studio integration and CSV exports
Multi-country and multi-language tracking

name: Ranked AI
tagline: Fully managed AI SEO and PPC combining tracking software with a team that implements the work.
description: Ranked AI is a hybrid software-plus-service offering for search marketing. Its platform includes keyword and AI-prompt tracking, audits, backlink monitoring, and local heatmaps, while its team writes content, builds links, and implements on-page fixes. Plans are month-to-month starting at $99 per website, with white-label options for agencies.
pricing_details: Standard $99/mo per website (25 target keywords, 1 article/week), Plus $198/mo (50 keywords, 2 articles/week), Enterprise $349/mo (100 keywords, 4 articles/week, dedicated account executive). Month-to-month with a free trial and no contracts.
use_cases: Outsourcing SEO execution for local and niche businesses
Tracking both traditional rankings and AI search visibility
Getting weekly blog content produced and published
Reselling SEO under an agency's own brand
Managing PPC campaigns with specialist oversight
pros: Service included, not just software dashboards
Low entry price at $99/mo with no contracts
No-limits keyword and prompt tracking on all plans
White-label option for agencies
cons: Priced per website, so multi-site costs scale linearly
Content output volume is capped per plan tier
Hybrid model means results depend on the assigned team
who_its_for: Small and local businesses without in-house SEO staff
Multi-location businesses needing managed search
Agencies wanting a white-label SEO stack
Teams wanting both AI visibility tracking and execution
key_features: Unlimited keyword and AI prompt tracking
Weekly managed blog content and web copy
On-page optimization and backlink acquisition
Local heatmaps and GBP management
GA, GSC, and GBP integrations
White-label dashboard, reports, and client portal

name: Subscribr
tagline: AI assistant for YouTube that finds outlier video ideas and writes scripts in your channel's voice.
description: Subscribr is a YouTube-focused AI tool that analyzes a creator's channel and niche to surface data-backed video ideas ranked by outlier performance, then generates ready-to-film scripts with hooks, structure, and retention-focused pacing. It also offers competitor channel tracking, an AI thumbnail generator, and voice matching trained on the creator's existing content. Billing is annual only, with a low-cost 7-day trial.
pricing_details: Annual billing only; the Creator plan is listed at $299/year on the site's checkout. New users can start with a $7 trial for the first 7 days, and a 30-day money-back guarantee is offered.
use_cases: Generating YouTube video ideas based on outlier data
Writing long-form scripts that match a creator's voice
Tracking competitor channels for topic opportunities
Producing thumbnails from script concepts
Speeding up pre-production for faceless channels
pros: Purpose-built for YouTube rather than generic AI writing
Idea generation grounded in live outlier video data
Voice matching keeps scripts on-brand
Low-risk $7 trial and 30-day refund policy
cons: Annual billing only; no monthly subscription option
Optimized for English; other languages need manual polish
Focused on pre-production, no editing or publishing tools
who_its_for: YouTube creators publishing long-form content
Faceless channel operators producing at volume
Video marketers scripting educational or story content
Creators who struggle with topic research and hooks
key_features: Outlier video idea generator using live YouTube data
Script writing with hooks, structure, and outros
Voice matching trained on the user's channel
Competitor channel tracking
AI thumbnail generation from script ideas
Built-in research agents with web search

name: Typa
tagline: AI content engine that drafts on-brand social posts from voice notes, links, and your knowledge base.
description: Typa is an AI content platform that learns a brand's voice and opinions, then drafts and schedules posts for X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, and Medium. Users can reach it through iMessage, Slack, voice calls, or the web app, and every draft waits for human approval before publishing. A self-updating knowledge base keeps research and drafts grounded in the company's actual material.
pricing_details: Free plan at $0/mo with $3 of usage credits. Pro is $17/mo plus $10 per connected social account (one connection included). A managed 'Founder Mode' ghostwriting service is available at custom pricing.
use_cases: Drafting social posts that match a founder's voice
Turning voice notes and links into publishable threads
Scheduling content across X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, and Medium
Maintaining a knowledge base that informs drafts
Delegating content review workflows to a team channel
pros: Voice cloning produces drafts that read authentically
Works inside iMessage, Slack, and voice calls
Human approval required before anything posts
Generous free entry point for testing
cons: Per-account connection fees add to the base subscription
Publishing coverage limited to a few text-first platforms
Young product with a small public track record
who_its_for: Founders and executives building a personal brand
Small marketing teams running social content
Creators who think out loud and want drafts from voice notes
Brands wanting ghostwriting with approval control
key_features: Brand voice matching across all drafts
Drafting from voice notes, links, and research
Multi-surface access: iMessage, Slack, voice, web
Approval workflow; nothing auto-publishes
Self-updating knowledge base
Scheduling to X, LinkedIn, Bluesky, and Medium

name: Riverflow
tagline: AI creative platform that generates on-brand images, videos, and ads trained on your visual identity.
description: Riverflow is an AI creative tool for marketing teams that trains on a brand's visual identity, values, and products to generate consistent campaign assets. It produces product photography-style images, static ads, and videos for channels like Meta, TikTok, email, and print, with a credit-based pricing model and commercial usage rights. An MCP integration lets teams generate assets from Claude, ChatGPT, or Codex.
pricing_details: Free plan with 50 credits/day for one brand. Paid plans per the official help center: Starter $39/mo ($29/mo annual, 2,250 credits), Growth $99/mo ($74/mo annual, 6,000 credits), Scale $249/mo ($187/mo annual, 16,000 credits), Enterprise custom.
use_cases: Generating on-brand product photography without shoots
Producing static ads and videos for paid social campaigns
Scaling creative output across multiple brands
Creating campaign assets in hours instead of weeks
Generating visuals directly from AI chat tools via MCP
pros: Brand training keeps outputs visually consistent
Covers images, static ads, and video in one credit system
Commercial usage rights included on all plans
Free daily-credit plan for evaluation
cons: Credit math differs per asset type, complicating budgeting
Lower tiers cap brand profiles and custom styles
Best results require upfront brand training effort
who_its_for: E-commerce and consumer brand marketing teams
Agencies producing ad creative for multiple brands
Growth teams iterating on paid social creative
Creative teams replacing routine photoshoots
key_features: Custom brand training on visual identity and products
Image, static ad, and video generation
Campaign-ready output for Meta, TikTok, email, and print
MCP connection to Claude, ChatGPT, and Codex
Custom scene and style training
Expert artworking support on higher tiers

name: intellijend
tagline: Music marketing platform that runs optimized Meta ads and tracks Spotify popularity scores for artists.
description: intellijend is a marketing automation platform for independent musicians that builds and optimizes Meta (Facebook/Instagram) ad campaigns aimed at streaming growth. It front-loads ad spend around releases, tests multiple creatives with automatic pausing of underperformers, and tracks Spotify's internal popularity scores to time algorithmic playlist pushes. The company reports usage by over 10,000 artists.
pricing_details: Subscription from $24.99/month, with Meta ad spend billed separately (the platform's guidance centers on roughly $10/day campaign budgets). Annual subscribers receive monthly ad creative packs.
use_cases: Launching Meta ad campaigns for new music releases
Triggering Spotify algorithmic playlists with timed ad spend
Tracking Spotify popularity scores release-over-release
Testing ad creatives systematically without Meta Ads Manager expertise
Growing monthly listeners as an independent artist
pros: Purpose-built for music promotion, not generic ad tooling
Automates Meta campaign structure and creative testing
Surfaces Spotify popularity data that is otherwise hidden
Strong user reviews for support and results
cons: Total cost requires meaningful ad spend on top of the subscription
Results depend heavily on music quality and creative
Narrow focus; only useful for streaming-focused music marketing
who_its_for: Independent artists releasing music regularly
Artist managers running release campaigns
Small labels promoting streaming growth
Musicians without Meta Ads Manager experience
key_features: Automated Meta ads campaign creation for music
Front-loaded release-day budget strategy
Spotify popularity score tracking
Multi-creative ad testing with auto-optimization
Ad spend overlayed on streaming metrics
Educational guides on Spotify algorithm mechanics
